# Known-failing tests on main. See docs/decisions/ADR-003-required-test-aggregator.md
#
# 2026-08-03: -111 entries, DELETED because they now pass (the ratchet's own
# prescribed action). Measured, not assumed: junit from the passing run
# (30840921840) vs the failing one (30841832328) on trees differing by TWO test
# functions gave 111 fail->pass and **0 newly failing**. So nothing regressed;
# execution order shifted and 111 tests stopped being poisoned.
#
# The poisoning is real and visible in the messages those tests carried while
# failing -- `ValueError: invalid literal for int(): 'https://github.com/x/x/pull/99'`
# and `FileNotFoundError: /tmp/pytest-of-runner/pytest-0/test_exact_decision_ap...`
# are one test receiving ANOTHER test's stubbed subprocess result and tmpdir.
# The suite leaks state in SERIAL, not only under xdist as previously recorded.
#
# They are deleted rather than marked `flaky`. `flaky` exempts an entry from the
# ratchet in BOTH directions, which would hide any genuine future regression in
# all 111; deletion keeps them protected and states the truth, which is that they
# pass on main today. The cost is that a future PR which shifts collection order
# again may see some of them fail and be blocked for something it did not cause.
# That cost is accepted only because the isolation fix is the next lane -- it is
# not a stable end state. Root cause and fix: the process-global state leak
# tracked in scripts/ci_required_tests.py's SERIAL ON PURPOSE note.
# Baseline captured 2026-08-02 from CI run 30767266528 (12,747 ran / 483 failing).
# One-way ratchet: entries that pass get DELETED by the gate; additions to this
# file require an exact-head review receipt (pr-scope-guard).
# 2026-08-03: +1 entry — tests/load/test_agent_runtime_cloud_load.py arrived on
# main after the baseline capture, already failing. Pre-existing debt, recorded
# honestly so it is counted; owner lane is the cloud-drain load work.
# code change. `flaky` exempts them from the stale ratchet in BOTH
#
# 2026-08-03: +141 entries from CI run 30780762657 (first push:main run).
# These are REAL regressions carried in by code that landed on main, not
# ordering artifacts -- verified: every failure the 53-file-exclusion run
# reported was ALSO failing in the same-tree full run, so the exclusion
# caused none of them. Recorded as ordinary ratcheted entries so a later
# fix shows up as a stale line that must be deleted.
